adaptation: GDP per capita, life expectancy and population replace health indicators.
finding: Bubble area is bounded by an explicit size range; country population is not squared.
chart_choice: Scatterplot position compares two numeric measures; population is the bubble area.

adaptation: Use population totals and GDP per capita; no outbreak count or district boundaries exist.
finding: No choropleth or disease-rate claim can be made from this dataset.
chart_choice: Sorted horizontal bars compare continent categories without implying geographic shape.

adaptation: Show GDP per capita scaling and the effect of a high outlier.
chart_choice: A scatterplot shows GDP per capita against its scaled value.

adaptation: Compare numeric-axis order in a parallel-coordinates chart.
finding: Greedy correlation order: lifeExp -> gdpPercap -> gdp_total -> pop.
chart_choice: Parallel coordinates show multiple numeric measures and make order effects visible.

adaptation: Quantile-classify the observed life-expectancy values, not disease rates.
finding: Range=39.6–82.6 years; classes are not evidence of five natural groups.
chart_choice: A sequential colour scale encodes ordered life-expectancy percentiles.

adaptation: Use population size to discuss denominator caution, not a fabricated disease rate.
finding: No case counts or Poisson rate estimates are available.
chart_choice: A log-scaled scatter shows population and GDP per person without calling either a disease rate.

adaptation: Compare country and continent-mean association of GDP and life expectancy.
chart_choice: Paired scatterplots keep country-level and continent-level associations distinct.

adaptation: Replace the land-area choropleth with a categorical population comparison.
finding: No area share, map projection, or geographic hotspot can be computed.
chart_choice: A sorted bar chart compares categories because no spatial geometry is available.

adaptation: Compare continent profiles on six normalized Gapminder indicators.
finding: Radar polygon area depends on axis order; it is not a reliable overall score.
chart_choice: A radar chart is retained only to demonstrate its area/order limitation, not to rank regions.
